qa.title: Q1372 (Jul. 18, 2025)
qa.question: What does 'give control' mean?
qa.answer:
Giving control of a card means moving it from your field to the field of an opponent who then becomes its new controller, allowing them to use it and its abilities.

When the given follower moves from the field to another zone, it returns to its owner's play area. For example, if it were to be put into the cemetery from the field, it would go into its owner's cemetery.

qa.title: Q1383 (Jul. 18, 2025)
qa.question: My opponent has an Ancient Protector on the field and their leader has 2 or less defense. My Shiva's "At the start of your end phase" ability triggers, and I select their leader and deal it 2 damage. Also, the number of faceup cards in my evolve deck has now reached 20 or more. Does either the damage or Shiva's "you win the game" ability cause me to win the game?
qa.answer:
No, the game continues. When an ability and an effect that restricts that ability are simultaneously in play, the restriction always takes precedence.

In this case, Ancient Protector's "you can't lose the game, and opponents can't win" ability would prevent Shiva's "you win the game" ability.

Additionally, because Shiva's damage and "you win the game" effect are part of the same ability, it would resolve in its entirety before moving on to the resolution of Ancient Protector's "When your leader's defense becomes 0 or less, put this card into its owner's cemetery and change your leader's defense to 1" ability.

qa.answer: No. When an ability requires a selection, the selection must be made before you resolve the other effects in the written order. In this case, before you draw a card, you must select an enemy follower (you may also select no enemy followers).

qa.title: Q862 (Aug. 8, 2024)
qa.question: If I have multiple cards with an "At the start of your end phase" ability triggering, in what order do I resolve them?
qa.answer: You can resolve them in any order. When you proceed to your end phase, all "At the start of your end phase" abilities are triggered and become pending. Then, you can choose the order in which you resolve the pending abilities.

qa.title: Q1125 (Jan. 31, 2025)
qa.question: If I search my deck with this follower's Fanfare ability, do I still have to reveal the card I searched for?
qa.answer: No. Whenever instructed to search for a card with specific features, you have to reveal it to prove that it meets the conditions specified. However, since this follower's Fanfare ability does not specify the kind of card, you don't have to reveal it.

qa.title: Q1124 (Jan. 31, 2025)
qa.question: When playing this follower's Fanfare ability, can I choose not to add a card to my hand?
qa.answer: No. Whenever instructed to search for a card, if the only condition specified is the number of cards, you must find that number of cards. Since this follower's Fanfare ability specifies to search your deck for any card, if your deck has at least 1 card you must search for 1 and add it to your hand.

qa.title: Q723 (Jun. 14, 2024)
qa.question: Does this amulet's ability mean my leader can't take more than a total of 4 damage on the turn I activate it?
qa.answer:
No. Any single instance of damage greater than 4 dealt to your leader that turn is reduced to 4.

For example, if your leader takes 5 damage twice, both instances are reduced to 4 for a total of 8 damage. If your leader takes 6 damage and then 3 damage, the first instance is reduced to 4 and the second is unaffected, giving a total of 7 damage.
